name: Air-popped popcorn
description: Plain popcorn kernels popped with hot air and a pinch of salt.
explanation: Just corn and salt. Butter and cheese toppings are where it stops being vegan.

name: Classic hummus
description: Creamy dip of chickpeas, tahini, lemon, garlic and olive oil.
explanation: All plant ingredients. Check flavored tubs for added dairy or meat toppings.

name: Plain rolled oats
description: A canister of old-fashioned oats, nothing added.
explanation: Oats are a grain with no animal ingredients. Instant packets are the ones that may add milk powder.

name: Firm tofu
description: A block of pressed soybean curd from the refrigerated aisle.
explanation: Made from soybeans, water and a coagulant such as calcium sulfate.

name: Extra virgin olive oil
description: Cold-pressed oil from olives.
explanation: Pressed olives and nothing else.

name: Plain tortilla chips
description: Salted corn chips: corn, vegetable oil and salt.
explanation: Corn, oil and salt. Flavored versions often add milk or cheese powders.

name: Canned chickpeas
description: Chickpeas, water and salt in a can.
explanation: Plain canned beans are plant-based. (Refried beans are the ones that may contain lard.)

name: Canned coconut milk
description: Thick, creamy milk pressed from coconut flesh.
explanation: Coconut and water, usually with a plant-based thickener.

name: Fresh guacamole
description: Mashed avocado with onion, cilantro, lime and salt.
explanation: All plants. Some restaurants and store-bought tubs add sour cream or mayo.

name: Plain white rice
description: Long-grain white rice, cooked in water.
explanation: A grain cooked in water. Restaurant rice may be cooked in chicken stock or butter.

name: Soy sauce
description: Dark, salty sauce for sushi and stir-fries.
explanation: Brewed from soybeans, wheat, salt and water.

name: Tempeh
description: Fermented soybean cake with a nutty flavor.
explanation: Soybeans fermented with a mold culture. No animal products.

name: Dried apricots
description: Chewy orange fruit, sold unsweetened in a bag.
explanation: Just fruit, usually preserved with sulfur dioxide.

name: Black coffee
description: A plain brewed cup, no milk or sugar.
explanation: Water and coffee beans.

name: Store-bought bagel
description: A plain bagel from the bread aisle.
explanation: The recipe is plant-based, but some dough conditioners use L-cysteine, which can come from feathers or hair, and the sugar may be bone-char filtered.

name: Lager beer
description: A standard supermarket six-pack of lager.
explanation: Beer is grain, hops, water and yeast, but some brewers clarify with isinglass (fish bladder) and it isn't listed on the label.

name: Brown sugar
description: Soft, moist sugar for cookies and oatmeal.
explanation: It's refined cane sugar with molasses added, and cane sugar may be filtered through bone char.

name: Clear apple juice
description: Bright, see-through apple juice in a carton.
explanation: Juice is just apples, but some producers clarify it with gelatin or isinglass, which doesn't appear on the label.

name: Sriracha hot sauce
description: Garlicky red chili sauce in a squeeze bottle.
explanation: Chili, garlic, vinegar, salt and sugar. No animal ingredients, but the sugar may be bone-char filtered.

name: Tomato ketchup
description: The classic table condiment for fries.
explanation: Made from tomatoes, vinegar, spices and sweetener, with no animal ingredients. The sugar and 'natural flavors' keep it from being a sure thing.

name: Creamy peanut butter
description: Standard supermarket jar with peanuts, sugar and oil.
explanation: No animal ingredients, but the added sugar may have been refined with bone char.

name: Sweetened dried cranberries
description: Tart red berries, dried with added sugar.
explanation: Fruit plus sugar, so bone char is a possibility. Some brands also coat them in a glaze that may be shellac.

name: Frosted corn flakes
description: Crunchy sweetened breakfast cereal, vitamin-fortified.
explanation: The recipe is plant-based, but the added vitamin D3 is often from lanolin (sheep's wool) and the sugar may be bone-char filtered.

name: Sweetened almond milk
description: A carton of vanilla almond milk from the fridge aisle.
explanation: Almonds, water and sugar, but the added vitamin D3 can come from lanolin, and the sugar may be bone-char filtered.

name: Hard pretzels
description: Crunchy salted twists in a snack bag.
explanation: Usually flour, yeast and salt, but some brands use L-cysteine or a little sugar or dairy.

name: Sandwich bread
description: A sliced white loaf from the bread aisle.
explanation: Plant-based at its core, but some loaves include mono- and diglycerides (which can be animal-derived), L-cysteine, or bone-char sugar.

name: Mango sorbet
description: A frozen, dairy-free fruit dessert.
explanation: Fruit, water and sugar. Sorbet has no dairy, but the sugar may be bone-char filtered and some brands add honey.

name: Jelly beans
description: Shiny, colorful, chewy candies in a bag.
explanation: Most are polished with confectioner's glaze (shellac, made from lac insects) and some reds are colored with carmine from insects.

name: Gummy fruit snacks
description: Chewy fruit-shaped candies in a pouch.
explanation: Most are made with gelatin, which comes from animal bones and skin.

name: Parmesan cheese
description: A hard, salty Italian cheese, grated over pasta.
explanation: Dairy, and traditional parmesan is also made with animal rennet from calf stomachs.

name: Caesar dressing
description: Creamy, garlicky dressing for romaine lettuce.
explanation: Classic recipes contain anchovies plus egg yolk and parmesan.

name: Fish sauce
description: A salty, savory sauce used all over Southeast Asian cooking.
explanation: Made from fermented fish, usually anchovies.

name: Mayonnaise
description: A creamy white spread for sandwiches.
explanation: Traditional mayo is oil emulsified with egg yolks. Vegan versions exist but are labeled as such.

name: Traditional kimchi
description: Spicy fermented napa cabbage from a Korean grocery.
explanation: Traditional recipes use fish sauce or salted shrimp. Vegan kimchi exists, but it's usually labeled.

name: Pad thai
description: Stir-fried rice noodles with peanuts and tamarind.
explanation: The classic dish includes egg, fish sauce and often dried shrimp.

name: Milk chocolate bar
description: A smooth, sweet candy bar.
explanation: Milk chocolate contains milk solids.

name: Greek yogurt
description: Thick, tangy strained yogurt in a tub.
explanation: It's made from cow's milk.

name: Caramel candies
description: Soft, chewy golden caramels in twisted wrappers.
explanation: Traditional caramel is made with butter and cream.

name: Butter croissant
description: A flaky, golden French pastry.
explanation: Its flaky layers come from butter, and it's usually brushed with egg wash.

name: Miso soup
description: A warm Japanese soup served with sushi.
explanation: Most miso soup is built on dashi, a broth made from dried bonito (fish).
